answer: A verifiable capacity protocol curtails Sybil attacks by requiring agents to dedicate pre-computed storage sectors over time. To authenticate a new state vertex, nodes whisper cryptographic proofs across peer links by reading index lookups from a dense marble allocation table. An adversary must expend scarce, persistent non-volatile disk space per simulated participant. However, large data centers with surplus storage can subsidize fake identities at negligible marginal cost.
